Asamyutha_Hasthas.pdf.text:
Anandamayi Nrityalaya
1. Asamyuta Hasthas (one-hand gesture)
Hastas / Mudras (hand gestures) are primarily classified as 28 Asamyuta 
Hastas (one-hand gesture). Each of the hasta can be used to denote various 
thoughts, ideas and objects.
Sloka:
Pathakaha Tripathakordhapathakaha Kartharimukhaha
Mayoorakhyordhachandrascha pyaraalaha Shukathundakaha
Mushtischa Shikharakhyascha Kapithaha Katakhamukhaha
Suchi Chandrakhala Padmakosha Sarpa shirshasthadha 
Mrugashirshaha Simhamukhaha Kaangoolaschalapadmakaha
Chaturo Bhramaraschaiva Hamsasyo Hamsapakshakaha
Samdamsho Mukulaschaiva Thaamrachoodah Trisoolakaha
Ithya samyutha Hasthana mashta vimshati reerita
Hastas:
1. Pathaka- When the thumb is bent and other fingers are held closely together and 
stretched, it is Pathaka Hasta.

2. Thripathaka- When the ring finger of pathaka hastha is bent, it 
becomes,Tripathaka Hastha. 
 
3. Ardhapathaka- When the little finger of Tripathaka hastha is bent, it becomes 
Ardhapathaka Hastha.
          
4. Kartarimukha- When the forefinger and the little finger of Tripathaka Hastha are 
extended back, it becomes Kartarimukha Hastha.
           
5. Mayura- If, in Tripathaka hastha, ring finger and the thumb are joined at the tips 
and other fingers are extended, it will be Mayura Hastha.

6. Ardhachandra- If the thumb of the Pathaka hastha is stretched out, it becomes 
Ardhachandra Hastha.
 
7. Arala- If the forefinger of Pathaka hastha is bent, then it becomes Arala Hastha.
          
8. Sukatunda- When the ring finger in Arala hastha is bent (fore finger is already 
bent), it becomes Sukatunda Hasta.
          
  
9. Mushti- All the four fingers should be folded and the thumb placed on them, then it 
is Mushti Hastha.

10.Shikhara- If the thumb of the Mushti Hasta is raised, it will be Shikara Hasta.
            
11.Kapittha- When the forefinger of the Sikhara hastha is bent over the top of the 
thumb, it becomes Kapitha Hastha.
            
12.Katakamukha-When the forefinger and the middle finger joined the thumb and 
the ring finger and last finger are stretched, it becomes Katakamukha Hastha.
13.Soochi- When the forefinger of Katakamukha hasta is upraised, it becomes Soochi 
Hastha.

14.Chandrakala- If the thumb of the Soochi hastha is released wide apart, it becomes 
Chandrakala Hastha.
          
15.Padmakosha- All the five fingers are separated and slightly bent and the palm is 
hollowed, then it is Padmakosa Hasta.
          
  
16.Sarpasheersha-If the ends of all the fingers of the Pataka hastha are bent, i.e., if 
the palm of the Pataka Hasta is hollowed, it becomes Sarpasheersha Hasta.
           
17.Mrugasheersha- If the little finger and the thumb of the Sarpaseersha hastha are 
extended, it becomes Mrugasheersha Hasta.

18.Simhamukha- When the tips of the middle finger and the ring finger are bent to 
touch the thumb and the rest are extended, it becomes Simhamukha Hasta.
           
   
19.Kaangula- If the ring finger of Padmakosa hastha is bent, it is Kaangula Hasta.
            
  
20.Alapadma- If all the fingers are stretched apart and the index finger stretched 
straight with the little finger bent inward, I becomes Alapadma Hasta. 
            
21.Chatura- When forefinger, middle finger and ring finger are close to one another 
and the stretched, the little finger is extended separately and the thumb is bent 
obliquely to touch the base of the ring finger, it becomes Chatura Hasta.

22.Bhramara- When the middle finger and the thumb meet each other, the forefinger 
is bent and the right finger and the little finger are stretched, it becomes Bhramara 
Hasta.
          
23.Hamsasya- When the three fingers i.e., middle, ring and little fingers are separated 
and extended, the tips of the forefinger and the thumb joined, then it becomes 
Hamsasya Hasta. 
 
24.Hamsapaksha- When the little finger of Sarpasirsha Hasta is extended, it becomes 
Hamsapaksha Hasta.
25.Samdamsha- When the fingers of Padmakosa hastha are repeatedly joined and 
separated, it becomes Samdamsa Hasta.

26.Mukula- When all the five fingers are joined together at the tips, it becomes 
Mukula Hasta.
           
   
27.Tamrachuda- If the forefinger of Mukula hastha is curved it becomes Tamrachuda 
Hasta.
            
28.Trishoola- If the thumb and the little finger of Pataka Hasta are held together, it 
becomes Trisula Hastha.

Drishti Bhedhas.pdf.text:
Drishti Bhedhas
EYE MOVEMENTS
Drishti means ”eyes” in sanskrit. The 8 eye movements refer to the eye positions when
expressing a particular bhava.
SLOKAM:
Sama malokitam Saachi pralokita Nimility
Ulloki ta-anu vrittechatathachai va-ava lokitam
Ithyashta drishti bhedaha syu kirtitah purvasuribhi
1. Sama: Eye kept still without any movement.
2. Alokita: Rolling your eye balls in a circular pattern.
3. Saachi: Looking through the corner of the eyes.
4. Pralokita: moving your eyes side to side.
5. Nimilita: It looks like a half shut eye. Here one tries to focus the eye ball towards the heart.
6. Ullokita: Looking upwards.
7. Anuvritta: Rapid movement of the eyes up and down.
8. Avalokita: Looking down.

Dvadasha Hasta Pranamas.pdf.text:
ANANDAMAYI NRITYALAYA
Dvadasha Hasta Pranamas
(12 Types of Hand Gesture Salutations)
Sloka:
Prasaranam Kunchitam Cha Rechitam Pumkhitam Thadha
Apa Veshti Takam Chapi Prerito Dveshṭito Thadha
Vyavritthah Parivritthashcha Sanketah Tadanantaram
Chihnam Padartha Tiketi Prana Dvadasha Hastajah
Meaning:
12 types of Pranamas (hand gesture salutations) are described for the hands. Hastas/Mudras
(hand gestures) are used in classical Indian dance to convey various thoughts, ideas and
expressions.
Hastas:
1. Prasaranam- Stretching the fingers outward.
2. Kunchitam- Bending or folding the fingers.
3. Rechitam- Moving/raising the fingers upward gently.
4. Pumkhitam- Shaking or spreading the fingers.
5. Apaveshṭitam- Bending the fingers of the hand downward.
6. Preritam- Spreading, moving, or stretching the fingers toward the back.
7. Udveshṭitam- Raising the hands upward during dance.
8. Vyavrittam- Lifting the hand sideways upward.
9. Parivritam- Bringing the hands forward from the side regions.
10. Sanketam- Gesturing/signaling without the use of words.
11. Chihnam- Representing direct and indirect objects (living and non-living things) through symbols
in a dance performance.
12. Padardha Tika- Demonstrating/showing objects through hand gestures.

Samyutha Hasthas.pdf.text:
2. Samyutha Hasthas (two-hand gestures)
Samyuta Hasta mudras or Combined hand gestures are expressions to be
shown by both hands. According to abhinaya darpanam there are 24
Samyuta hasta mudras.
Sloka:
Anjalischa kapothascha karkataha swastikasthadha
Dolahasthaha pushpaputa uthsungha sivalingakaha
Katakavardhanaschiva karthari swasthikasthadha
Sakataha shankachakroucha samputaha paasakeelakau
Matshyaha kurmo varahascha garudo nagabandhakaha
Khatva bherundakakascha avahithasthadhaivacha
Chaturvimshati sankyakhaha samyuthah kadithah karah
Hasthas:
1. Anjali- When two pataka hasthas are joined palm to palm, it becomes Anjali hastha.

2. Kapothamu- When the palms of Anjali hastha meet only at their side,base & top, it
becomes Kapootha hastha.
3. Karkatamu- When the fingers of both the hands are interlocked and the fingers are
turned inward towards palms or outwards, it becomes Karkata hastha.
4. Swasthikamu- When two pataka hasthas are held together across at the wrists, it
becomes Swasthika hastha.

5. Dola hastamu- When two pataka hasthas are places on the sides of the respective
thighs, it becomes Dola hastha.
6. Pushpaputamu- When two sarpasirsha hasthas are pressed together so that the
little fingers and wrists are joined, it becomes Pushpaputa hastha.
7. Uthsungamu- When two mrughasirsha hasthas are held on the opposite armpits or
upper arms, it becomes Uthsunga hastha.

8. Sivalingamu- When the right hand as shikara hastha is placed on the left hand
which is Ardhachandra hastha, it becomes Sivalinga hastha.
9. Katakavardhanamu- When two katakamukha hasthas are crossed at the wrists, it
becomes Katakavardhana hastha.
10.Karthariswasthikamu- When two kartarimukha hasthas are crossed at the wrists,
it becomes Kartari swasthika hashta.

11.Sakatamu- When the middle fingers and the thumbs of two bhramara hasthas are
extended (stretched) it becomes Sakata hastha.
12.Sankhamu- When the left thumb of ardhachandra hastha is held with sikhara
hastha on right hand, it becomes Sankha hastha.
13.Chakramu- When the palms of two ardhachandra hasthas are joined askew, it
becomes Chakra hastha.

14. Samputamu- If the fingers of both chakra hasthas are curved and held , it
becomes Samputa hastha.
15. Paasamu- When the index fingers of two soochi hasthas are bent and interlocked,
it becomes Paasa hastha.
16.Keelakamu- When the little fingers of two mrugasirsa hasthas are bent inwards and
interlocked, it becomes Keelaka hastha.

17.Matsyamu- When the palm of a pathaka hastha is placed on the back of other
pathaka hastha and the thumbs and the little fingers are out stretched it becomes
Matsya hastha.
18.Kurmamu- In chakra hastha, if the thumbs and the little fingers are extended and
the ends of the other fingers are bent, it becomes Kurma hastha.
19.Varahamu- When two mrugasirsha hasthas are placed one over the and their little
fingers and thumbs are linked, it is Varaha hastha.

20.Garudamu- When the palms of ardhachandra hasthas are held askew and the
thumbs are interlocked, it becomes Garuda hastha.
21.Nagabandhakamu- When the two sarpasirsha hasthas are in swastika position, it
becomes Nagabandha hastha.
22.Khatva- When the thumbs, middle and ring fingers of two chatura hasthas (held one
over the other) are extended and their ends meet, it becomes Khatva hastha.

23.Bherundamu- When the wrists of two kapittha hasthas are joined, it becomes
Bherunda hastha.
24.Avahithamu- If two alapadma hasthas are crossed and placed near the chest it
becomes Avahitha hastha.

Sapta Talamulu.pdf.text:
ANANDAMAYI NRITYALAYA
Sapta Talamulu - Kartalu - Pattika
(SevenTalas-Creators-Chart)
Sloka:
Dhruva Matya Rupakashcha Jhampeh Triputa Eva Cha
Ata Tala Eka Talashcha Sapta Talah Prakirtitah
The Seven Talas (Sapta Talamulu):
Tala Angamulu (Components) Pattern Note
1. Dhruva Tala Laghu,Dhrutam,Laghu,Laghu 1011 '1'=Laghu
2. Matya Tala Laghu,Dhrutam,Laghu 101 '0'=Dhrutam
3. Rupaka Tala Dhrutam,Laghu 01 'c'=Anudhrutam
4. Jhampe Tala Laghu,Anudhrutam,Dhrutam 1c0
5. Triputa Tala Laghu,Dhrutam,Dhrutam 100
6. Ata Tala Laghu,Laghu,Dhrutam,Dhrutam 1100
7. Eka Tala Laghu 1
Tala Kartalu (Creators of the Talas):
Theseventalaswerecreatedbythecombinedeffortsofmanygreatscholars.
Dhruva Tala Kartalu:BharatoDattishchaivaAnjaneyoMatodhruva
Meaning:Bharatacharya,Dattishi,andAnjaneyatogethercreatedDhruvaTala.
Matya Tala Kartalu:MatyaTalasyaKartaromutangarnusaKohala
Meaning:MatangaMaharshi,Arjuna,andKohalacharyudutogethercreatedMatyaTala.

ANANDAMAYI NRITYALAYA
Rupaka Tala Kartalu:AnjaneyaKumbhojiPiYajnavalkasthuRupake
Meaning:Anjaneya,Kumbhoja(Agastya),andYajnavalkyatogethercreatedRupakaTala.
Jhampe Tala Kartalu:NandishchaBharatashchaShanakaJhampayamchevasthadha
Meaning:Nandikeswara,Bharata,andShanakatogethercreatedJhampeTala.
Triputa Tala Kartalu:NishacharapatihiBrahmoTriputeShankhaPalaka
Meaning:Ravanudu,Brahma,andShankhaPaludutogethercreatedTriputaTala.
Ata Tala Kartalu:BalihiKumaraDevendraAtaTalaSamudbhava
Meaning:Balichakravarti,Devendra,andKumaraswamicreatedAtaTala.
Eka Tala Kartalu:MahatanchaapiSarveshamEkatalaSamamViduh
Meaning:Bytheagreementofallthegreatones,EkaTalawasformulated.
These seven talas, combined with five jaatis, form a total of 35 talas.

Shiro Bhedhas.pdf.text:
Shiro Bhedhas
HEAD MOVEMENTS
Shira or shirasa means ”head” in sanskrit. The 9 head movements refer to the head positions
when expressing a particular bhava.
SLOKA:
Sama Mudvahita Madhomukha m-alolitam Dhutam
kampitam cha paravritta Mukshiptam parivahitam
navdha kathitam sheersham Natyashastra visharadaihi
Explaination:
1. Sama : The head kept straight
MEANING: When the head is motionless or straight, not bent or raised.
2. Udvahitam : Head Looking upwards
MEANING: When the face is raised, it is in udvahita position
3. Adhomukham : Looking Down
MEANING: When the face is cast down, the head is in adhomukham position.
4. Alolitam: Circular Movement of the head
MEANING: When the head moves in a circle, it becomes alolitam sirah.
5. Dhutam: Right to left movement of the head
MEANING: When the head is moved from left to right and right to left, it is dhutam shirah.
6. Kampitam: Up and down nod of the head
MEANING: When the head is shaken up and down, it is called kampitam sirah.
7. Paravrittam: Brisk turning of the head to the right or left
MEANING: When the head is quickly turned to one side, it is called paraavrittam.
8. Ukshiptam: Head is turned and raised or a slanting position of the head.

MEANING: When the head is turned to a side and raised, it becomes utkshipta sirah.
9. Parivahittam: Quick small shakes of the head.
MEANING: When the head is moved side to side very fast, it is called Parivaahita.
